searches.note: Twenty five searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's, three left unspent. The four shared searches went to the DO Valdeorras (its pages and the Xunta's DOG for 1945 and the ReViVal of 1974), to the Ribeira Sacra orders twice (the DOG of 1996, the Xunta's DOP page, the BOE of 1997 and the order of 30 May 1995) and to the Bibei's course. The houses' own domains were searched by restriction three times (rafaelpalacios.com, guitianvinos.com, adegaalgueira.com), each read as primary through its summary; the rest went to the open web with the author's sources blocked (the houses' domains, Liberty Wines, Berry Bros., Spanish Wine Lover, Vozpópuli, Gourmet Hunters, En Copa de Balón, Bodeboca, Skurnik, Wine.com, Vinetur, Ultracomida) so that an independent account could be heard. No fetch tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the DO and its orders, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the governing texts (the DOG and the BOE for Ribeira Sacra, the DO Valdeorras's pages and the Xunta's resolution, the accounts of the DO Ribeiro), then to independent accounts of each house's dates and people, then to merchants' and importers' sheets of each wine for the blend, the months and the vessels, the author's sources blocked.

Where the sheets disagreed and none was primary, the figure was widened to what the sheets give or hedged; where a fact rested on one account and the refuter found it nowhere (destemming, the Burgundy casks, the textile trade, Pizarra's vineyard, the Chardonnay and Cabernet line, a young Algueira Mencía), it was taken out.

tested: The making of As Sortes, the house's domain and the author's merchants blocked: Gourmet Hunters and Millesima give fermentation in 500 litre French oak barrels and about eight months on fine lees, Millesima native yeasts; Sobre Lías gives six old parcels on the north slope of the Bibei at about 680 metres on sandy granite. Borne out. Verema's vertical shows the 2005 fermented in 3,000 litre foudres and the 500 litre barrels coming later, which is why the library says large wood.

The house's own pages, searched on its domain: six sortes planted by local growers in the late 1970s and early 1980s and bought between 2004 and 2007, on the north face of the Bibei valley at Santa Cruz do Bolo above 680 metres, Godello of about forty years on average, 500 litre barrels and eight months; O Soro a sorte planted on terraces in 1978 and made the same way; the history page's start in 2004 buying old Godello from aged growers, and the sorte inherited by draw. Borne out, save the sites' claim that the sortes are the house's oldest vines.

The oldest vineyard: the house's Antiga page, Vinos con Carácter and Songbird give Sorte Antiga, planted in 1920 on its own roots as bush vines, as the oldest vineyard the house owns, so the sites' claim was wrong. Sorte Antiga is fermented on its skins in open oak vats by the same pages.

The founding and the family: Polaner Selections gives the leaving of the family's Rioja estate in 2004, the buying of old Godello from older growers and the meaning of sorte, a plot inherited by drawing lots. Borne out; Louro do Bolo from younger vines in 35 hectolitre foudres for four months on fine lees by Polaner.

The drinking window: Decanter and Sokolin give 2020 to 2039 for the 2019, Grand Cru Wijnen 2026 to 2032 for the 2024, Lay Wheeler a window to 2034 for the 2023. Nobody gives five years before it opens; the ageing line was changed.

The ReViVal plan and the DO: 1974 by the Xunta's DOG of 2024 and by the DO's fiftieth year of the plan in 2024, 1975 on another of the DO's pages; Galicia's second oldest denomination, qualified on 27 July 1945, by the DO's own page. The record's 1974 and its hedge stand.

The Bibei's course, for the trap: Turismo de Galicia and a table of Galicia's rivers give the river rising in Zamora and running through Viana do Bolo, O Bolo, Manzaneda and A Pobra de Trives to the Sil, so Manzaneda lies downstream of O Bolo and the trap's upstream was wrong.

The house rules: nobody living named (the house keeps its name; the founder is said as a younger member of the family), no price, no score (the scores met in the results are not used), nothing volatile (the 24.5 hectares and 32 sortes met in one result are not used), British, no dash.

open: The ReViVal's first year: 1974 by the Xunta's DOG of 2024 and the DO's fiftieth year in 2024, 1975 on another DO page; the record keeps 1974.

The library's large wood for As Sortes: true of the first vintages (the 2005 in 3,000 litre foudres by Verema's vertical), while the house's page gives 500 litre barrels; the vintage of the change was not found.
Louro's little Treixadura rests on the library in what the refuter read; Polaner gives Louro do Bolo from younger vines in 35 hectolitre foudres for four months on fine lees.
The years in the family's Rioja firm rest on the author's two merchants and Polaner's leaving of the Rioja estate in 2004; Plácet stays out.

tested: The founding and the family, the author's sources blocked: Albariño.com, Bodeboca, Enterwine and Drinks&Co give the brothers' project of 1985 on the family estate at Rubiá de Valdeorras, led by one brother, who died in a road accident (late in 1996 by one account); his brother and sister carry it on. Borne out.

The house's own pages, found by restriction to guitianvinos.com (the author found none): the Godello planted in 1985 from a very old clone, the two oenologists who have made the wines since the founding (so with consulting oenologists from the start stands), most wines in steel with a smaller part in French and American oak and a very little in acacia, the house's claim to have pioneered in Spain a wine kept on its lees without wood, and the Vendimia Tardía, a sweet Godello of 2011 picked near Christmas. Borne out.

The first barrel fermented Godello: Guitián Fermentado en Barrica 1996 told as the first in the world by one account, barrel trials by the oenologist in 1994 by another, a first Guitián of 1992 by two; the record's middle of the 1990s, told as the house's claim, stands.

The making of Sobre Lías, the author's merchants blocked: El Gusto por el Vino, Vinos Baco and Alforins give 100 per cent Godello fermented in steel at 16 to 18 degrees, four to six months on its lees in tank (six for some vintages), the lees stirred weekly, and at least two months in bottle. Borne out; the weekly stirring, left out by the author for want of a second source, now has three and is added.
The Valdeorras label line: the DO's own page gives the Sil, Xares and Bibei; from O Barco to A Rúa left out Rubiá, which lies up the Sil from O Barco towards Bierzo, so the line was changed.

The house rules: nobody living named (the brother who led the house is described, the sister and brother who carry it on and the two oenologists are not named), no price, no score, nothing volatile (the nine or ten hectares met are not used), British, no dash.

The first wine and the winery building: 1992 by two accounts for the first Guitián, 1995 or the early 1990s for the building; neither is stated in the record.
The brother's death: late 1996 by one account, about ten years after the founding by another; his dates were found nowhere, so he stays described.

tested: The history, the house's domain and the author's merchants blocked: the Consejo's directory, Antalva, Decanter, Enterwine and Gourmet Hunters give the first vineyard of 1979, abandoned stone terraces restored by hand, the building of 1996 (the Consejo, Enterwine), the brand of 1998 (Antalva, Gourmet Hunters) and a founding of 2005 (Decanter). Founded stays empty, as the author left it.

The vineyard's name: two results that quote the house (PrivateCeller's sheet of Algueira Fincas, a catalogue) give Carballo Cobo, the first vineyard of 1979, then abandoned, half destroyed terraces on a steep slope; Carballocovo, the author's spelling, was met in no result. Changed to Carballo Cobo and left open.

The making of Pizarra, the author's merchants blocked: Vinos con Carácter gives twelve to eighteen months in French oak, barrels and foudres, then tank; Xadigal twelve for the 2015, a sheet thirteen for the 2016, Gourmet Hunters twelve for the 2017, Dicomar eighteen in foudres and casks. The house's own sheet gives fourteen months in French oak for the 2017, Mencía alone, slate, facing south. Twelve to fourteen was too narrow and was changed.
The grapes: Mencía alone on the house's sheet and Vinos con Carácter, from old vines by Antalva; Liberty's blend with Brancellao and Caíño for a recent vintage keeps alone or very nearly so.

The sites: the house's sheets give slate and a south aspect for Pizarra and Doade a south facing slope of slate; the importer's Carballocovo as Pizarra's source rests on one account, and Antalva calls it a single vineyard without a name, so it was cut.

The other wines, on the house's own pages: Carravel, Mencía alone from chosen plots of Doade each fermented apart and aged in French oak; Risco, Merenzao alone on gneiss and slate facing south west; Serradelo, Brancellao on schist, slate and gneiss facing south; Fincas, Caíño and Sousón. The author's Algueira Mencía, a young red, was found on no page read and was replaced.

The DO: the Xunta's DOG gives the recognition of the DO Ribeira Sacra by an order of 30 May 1995 with a provisional council, its definitive recognition and its rules by the order of 3 September 1996 (DOG of 11 September 1996), and the Ministry's ratification of 11 September 1997 (BOE); the five subzones on several pages. Authorised on 3 September 1996 told half the story and was changed in the label, the story and the card.
The house rules: nobody living named (the founder, his wife and their son are said as the family), no price, no score, nothing volatile, British, no dash.

Pizarra's vineyard: Carballo Cobo by Liberty, Abeleda for part of a recent vintage by Liberty, a single vineyard of old vines by Antalva; not settled, so the record names none.
Founding: 1979 for the first vineyard, 1980 for the founder's arrival, 1996 for the building, 1998 for the brand, 2005 by Decanter; founded stays empty.
The founding member of the DO of 1996: one producer guide again (the same Wine Scholar Guild entry), so it stays out.
The fifteen centuries of vines at Doade: the house's account, Roman times by one importer; told as the house's.

tested: The founding, the author's sources blocked: the Consejo's directory and Galicia en Vinos place the house at Langullo in Manzaneda; one account gives a founding of 2002, another the Priorat consultants' help from 2002, Falstaff and Lay Wheeler 2001 or 2002. The author's 2000 or 2001 now reads 2000, 2001 or 2002; founded stays empty.

The founder: one importer calls him the brother of a fashion designer returning to his family's roots, another the estate's founders locals returning to theirs; the textile trade of the author's account was met in no result and was cut for the roots, as the importers tell it.

The range: the Consejo's directory and Galicia en Vinos list Lacima, Lalama, Lapena, Lapola and Dominio do Bibei, Lalama and Lacima red Mencía wines, Lapena and Lapola Godello based whites. The author's report that the house's white is Lapola and not Lapena is not borne out: both exist. Lalume is Ribeiro and led by Treixadura (Grape Expectations, Decantalo, Table Wine).

Lalama's grapes: about nine tenths Mencía with Brancellao, Mouratón, Sousón and Garnacha for the 2013 and 2022 (K&L Wines, Grape Expectations); Alicante Bouschet in the 2021 (Solowine and another sheet); Skurnik's Garnacha Tintorera. The grapes now say what the sheets say.

The making: K&L Wines gives fermentation in oak vats with native yeasts, the malolactic in 300 litre barrels, thirteen months there and seven more in oak vat for the 2013; Grape Expectations open vessels and twenty months in foudres for the 2022; another sheet fourteen months in old casks and six in tank for the 2014. Destemming and the older Burgundy casks rest on one source each and were cut; a year and more, up to about twenty months, stands.
The sites: slate and schist above all, granite and some clay; heights of 350 to 920, 300 to 700, up to 680 and 250 to 350 metres by different sheets. Changed to say so.
The DO: as for Algueira, recognised in 1995 and confirmed with its rules in 1996 by the DOG, so the story's authorised in 1996 was changed, and the story question's stem no longer asserts the year.

The house rules: nobody living named (the founder, his brother the designer and the Priorat consultants are not named), no price, no score, nothing volatile (the thirty hectares and the bottles a year met in one result are not used), British, no dash.

open: Which Garnacha: Garnacha on the 2013 and 2022 sheets, Alicante Bouschet on the 2021, Garnacha Tintorera on Skurnik; the record gives them as the sheets do.
The founding: 2000, 2001 or 2002; founded stays empty. The first vintage of 2002 rests on the author's two merchants, with a third account giving the consultants' help from 2002.
The heights: 350 to 920, 300 to 700, up to 680 and 250 to 350 metres by different sheets.
Lapena and Lapola: both Godello based whites by one listing; their blends were not settled.

tested: The co-operative, the author's sources blocked: Campo Galego, Xeodestino O Ribeiro and Enoturismo Spain give Vitivinícola del Ribeiro founded in 1968 by its growers, wines of Ribeiro and Valdeorras, and the co-operative as the first to seek the native grapes' return, paying its members for the grafting (Campo Galego). Borne out; the Chardonnay and Cabernet line of one account was cut for what two say.

The blend and the making, the author's sources blocked: Drinkfy, Valín and Drinks&Co give each variety fermented apart at low temperature in steel and blended after; the grapes Treixadura, Torrontés, Albariño, Godello and Loureira on Luintra Gourmet, Treixadura about seven tenths with Albariño, Godello and Torrontés on another sheet. Albariño is in more listings than the author's some vintages allowed, so the grapes were changed; the making no longer rests on one merchant.

The DO: the ordinances of 1579 (most accounts; 1594 in one), the protection of 1932 under the Estatuto del Vino made law on 26 May 1933, the council constituted on 6 December 1956 and its first rules of 31 July 1957 (Interempresas, El Español, Wikipedia). The story's by an order of 6 December 1956 was changed to formed on that day.

Colección 68: WineAlign, the Concours Mondial, Ultracomida and a shop listing give a blend of about 85 per cent Treixadura with Albariño and Godello or Loureira, not Treixadura alone, so the others line and the story were changed. That it is named for 1968 is in one account only.

The Torrontés trap: the Argentine government's report gives Torrontés Riojano as Muscat of Alexandria crossed with Criolla Chica and the efforts to tie it to Spain's Torrontés as fruitless; the DOCa Rioja page warns the Galician Torrontés is unrelated to Rioja's Turruntés and to Argentina's. The region record agrees. The trap stands, worded as a different variety.
The serve: 8 degrees on most sheets, 8 to 10 on Gula Galega; the record's 8 to 10 stands.

The house rules: nobody living named (the president, a founder's grandson, is not named), no price, no score, nothing volatile (the members, hectares, bottles and share of the DO met in the results are not used), British, no dash.

livingNote: None of these is named in the fragment's prose; the read together agent adds those it judges living to people.json. Rafael Palacios is the producer's own name, which people.json allows on the house's own record; listing him keeps him out of every other record. Described, never named, for want of dates in two sources: Ramón Guitián, the brother who led A Tapada and died late in 1996 by one account (long dead, but no birth year read), and the president of Viña Costeira, a founder's grandson.
swapNote: The author proposed no swap, and the refuter proposes none. Rafael Palacios's As Sortes, A Tapada's Guitián, Algueira's Pizarra, Dominio do Bibei's Lalama and Viña Costeira's white are each a real wine of a house of its own DO, and each stands on the house's own pages or two sheets. Godeval, the plan's alternative for A Tapada, is not needed: Guitián's founding, its family and its Sobre Lías are borne out by the house's own pages. Pizarra is not called the flagship by any page read, but it is the house's own Mencía of the slate and its most listed red; the thin region rule allows it, so the pick stands.
planNotes: rafael-palacios: answered. The label is As Sortes, Val do Bibei, Valdeorras; its six sortes, the planting by local growers in the late 1970s and early 1980s, Santa Cruz do Bolo and 680 metres are on the house's own page. The why's fermented and aged in large wood is loose: the house gives 500 litre barrels for As Sortes, the foudres belong to Louro and to the first vintages of As Sortes.

a-tapada: answered. The house is Bodegas A Tapada at Rubiá, founded in 1985 by the brothers' replanting with Godello, by the house's own pages and three accounts; the label taught is Guitián Godello Sobre Lías, with the barrel wine in others; no living member of the family is named.

algueira: answered. Founded stays empty (1979, 1980, 1996, 1998 and 2005 are all given); Pizarra is Mencía alone or very nearly so by the house's sheet and the merchants', and no page calls it the flagship; the native grape reds are the house's Risco (Merenzao), Serradelo (Brancellao) and Fincas (Caíño and Sousón). The why's one of the founding wineries of the DO of 1996 rests on one producer guide, and the DO was first recognised in 1995, so the why needs a change.

dominio-do-bibei: answered. The label is Lalama, Ribeira Sacra; its grapes Mencía with Brancellao, Mouratón, Sousón and a Garnacha the sheets give as Garnacha, Garnacha Tintorera or Alicante Bouschet; founded 2000, 2001 or 2002, so left empty; Lacima is the house's other red by the Consejo's directory and Galicia en Vinos. The house's whites are Lapena and Lapola both, so the plan note's Lapena was right and the author's correction of it was not.

vina-costeira: answered. The co-operative is Vitivinícola del Ribeiro, founded in 1968 by Campo Galego and the author's three accounts; that Colección 68 is named for the year rests on one account and stays out, and Colección 68 is a Treixadura led blend, not a Treixadura alone. The white's blend is Treixadura led with Torrontés, Godello, Albariño and Loureira; the record says it is a co-operative.
